topic: Scope label for the duration complement of last
claim: In [13ib], The strike didn’t last two days, the duration phrase is labelled an adjunct: “[negative has scope over adjunct]”.
evidence_summary: The prose below the display on p. 706 says “In [i] two days is part of the complementation of last”, and calls it the “duration dependent”. Page 703 [2ii] labels The staff meeting lasted (for) five hours “[complement: S orientation]”. Page 665 defines the term: “the term ‘adjunct’ covers modifiers in the VP or clause together with related supplements”.
finding: The label contradicts §7.1 and the prose beneath it on p. 706, which calls the phrase the “duration dependent”. Page 665’s definition excludes complements, so the label can’t be read as a cover term. Read “complement”, as in p. 703 [2ii].
inference: Is the duration phrase with last a complement or an adjunct?

evidence.example: The sentence after [13] on p. 706, and p. 703 [2ii].
evidence.establishes: The display label conflicts with the chapter’s own analysis of last.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.
